title: Memories of Mirador and Christ the Redeemer
primary_topics: Personal spiritual memoir of CJP and Leni's Marriage Encounter (ME) experience at Mirador Villa, Baguio -- May 1986 -- and its transformative effect on their marriage

The anonymous donation of the 'Christ the Redeemer' statue at the portico of the Mirador Shrine by CJP, Leni, and fellow BLD Treasury Ministry couples -- kept anonymous for 30 years until Fr. Jose Quilongquilong SJ found them in 2019
The ME experience: from a divided couple to 'a united whole that completely surrendered all cares and pains to our Lord' in the span of one weekend
Mirador as a site of resurrection and salvation: the couple's continuing 35-year witness that 'there is no problem so big God cannot solve it'
sub_topics: The flat-tire obstacle: en route to Mirador from Quezon City, the car had a flat tire; after replacing it with the spare, another tire blew; stranded in Tarlac for over an hour scouting for a new tire; arrived late apologizing; hosts congratulated them: 'the evil one usually visits couples going to Mirador with similar problems to discourage them from going farther'

Marriage Encounter Class 26: about 15 other couples; welcomed by BLD 'Praise Ministry' singing; small room with common bath and toilet; common dining room; little chapel with Blessed Sacrament exposed 24 hours a day with 'Intercessory Ministry' prayer

The 'auxiliaries': members of a previous ME class -- prominent in businesses, professions, government -- serving as cooks, waiters, ushers, singers and prayer warriors, 'unabashedly attending to our every need as the honored guests of a powerful and all-seeing King'

ME format: not pedantic classroom lectures but 'sharing of experiences' -- an 'A' couple (benign marital problems) and a 'B' couple (serious enough to separate for years until they found Christ in their own ME)

Fr. Pascual Adorable SJ: 'Lightning Rod of God'; his homily 'penetrated deep into our body, soul and spirit, starting with the five senses and later gnawed into our very being overcoming us completely into the holy presence of the Lord'

Transformation in one weekend: from a divided couple to 'a united whole that completely surrendered all cares and pains to our Lord, happy and confident that there is no problem so big God cannot solve it'
Three weeks after ME: returned to Mirador as volunteer couple-sponsors for Class 26's next batch, 'singing to them, serving them and praying for them, and sharing our own transformation in Christ'
BLD's continuing support: weekly prayer meetings, one-on-one shepherding, Life in the Spirit Seminar (LSS) -- all described in SC023 (Diamond Anniversary speech)
The Christ the Redeemer statue: built and donated by CJP, Leni and other BLD Treasury Ministry couples to the portico of the Mirador Shrine -- anonymously for 30 years

Discovery and rededication: Fr. Jose Quilongquilong SJ found them and asked them to 'come out in the open and relate how the statue was built'; on the 30th year of its donation, June 8, 2019, simple ceremonies re-dedicated it with a marker at its foot and a short scroll at the hallway of the Retreat House

Note on 'mid-life marital problems': CJP mentions them obliquely -- 'a couple-friend who knew of our mid-life marital problems' -- without specifying; the ME is the resolution, not the problem itself; the 35-year witness since then is the testimony

Their hosts' response -- congratulating them for 'gamely conquering our first obstacle' -- frames adversity on the path to spiritual growth as a predictable and confirmatory sign, not a deterrent.

stances.claim: The Marriage Encounter experience is not merely an emotional weekend retreat but a permanent transformation capable of resolving 'mid-life marital problems' that had divided a couple. one_paragraph_summary: Published September 20, 2020, this spiritual memoir by CJP narrates how he and Leni attended 'Marriage Encounter Class 26' at Mirador Villa, Baguio in May 1986 -- invited by a couple-friend who knew of their 'mid-life marital problems' -- and how the weekend transformed them from a divided couple to 'a united whole that completely surrendered all cares and pains to our Lord.' The journey itself began with a double flat tire: the car blew a tire en route from Quezon City; the spare also went flat; they were stranded in Tarlac for over an hour. When they arrived apologizing, their hosts congratulated them: 'the evil one usually visits couples going to Mirador with similar problems to discourage them from going farther.' ME Class 26 featured about 15 couples welcomed by BLD's Praise Ministry; a small room with shared facilities; a 24-hour Adoration chapel tended by the Intercessory Ministry; and the 'auxiliaries' -- prominent professionals and government figures from a previous ME class who served as cooks, waiters, ushers and prayer warriors. The ME format was not classroom lectures but the 'sharing of experiences' of two couples (one with benign problems, one who had separated before finding Christ), followed by the homily of Fr. Pascual Adorable SJ -- the 'Lightning Rod of God' -- whose words 'penetrated deep into our body, soul and spirit.' Three weeks later, CJP and Leni returned to Mirador as volunteer sponsor-couples for the next batch, 'singing to them, serving them and praying for them, and sharing our own transformation in Christ.' The central disclosure of the memoir is that CJP, Leni and fellow BLD Treasury Ministry couples built and donated the 'Christ the Redeemer' statue at the portico of the Mirador Shrine -- and kept the donation anonymous for 30 years until Fr. Jose Quilongquilong SJ found them and asked them to go public. On June 8, 2019 -- the 30th year -- simple ceremonies rededicated the statue with a marker at its foot and a short scroll at the Retreat House hallway. For CJP, Mirador is synonymous with resurrection and salvation: since 1986, 'we have never experienced any more problems that could not be overcome with prayers of surrender to our Lord Jesus Christ, who by His own suffering, death and resurrection made it possible for us to enjoy the joy of Christian marriage.'
